title: Belfast Is Burning. India's T20I Tour of Ireland May Not Survive It.
excerpt: Street violence and anti-immigration riots in Northern Ireland have forced Cricket Ireland to review the safety of hosting India at Stormont, with a decision expected within 48 hours
body:
India's upcoming two-match T20I series in Ireland is under a cloud of uncertainty after violent unrest in Belfast forced Cricket Ireland to review the safety of hosting international cricket in the Northern Irish capital.

Both T20I matches — scheduled for June 26 and 28 at Stormont Cricket Ground — were meant to mark India's first cricket appearance in Belfast since 2007. Instead, the assignment has triggered urgent security assessments after a wave of anti-immigration protests and street violence convulsed the city in recent days.

The disorder was sparked by a stabbing incident in which a 30-year-old Sudanese asylum seeker blinded a local man. What followed was an escalation that has seen up to 300 protesters burn cars, trucks, and shops near Belfast, with police deploying water cannons and other crowd-control measures. According to reports, 16 arrests have been made and at least 12 police officers have been injured.

## Cricket Ireland Weighs Its Options

Cricket Ireland issued a statement acknowledging the severity of the situation and confirmed it would decide within 48 hours whether to proceed with or relocate the India T20I fixtures.

"The safety and security of players, coaches, match officials, and supporters is paramount in our deliberations," the board said, adding that it is consulting with law enforcement and government authorities.

The governing body also placed its domestic Irish Senior Cup and National Cup fixtures under review while it assesses conditions across Belfast and wider Northern Ireland.

## What This Means for the BCCI

The BCCI is monitoring developments closely. India's squad for the Ireland tour features significant changes — Shreyas Iyer has been named the new T20I captain, replacing Suryakumar Yadav, with Tilak Varma as vice-captain. The squad also includes 15-year-old batting prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, whose selection generated considerable excitement among fans.

India's previous visits to Irish soil — including the 2023 tour — were all held at Malahide in Dublin's suburbs, a considerably quieter venue. The decision to host matches in Belfast was meant to broaden cricket's footprint in Northern Ireland, but the current crisis has made that ambition untenable without cast-iron security guarantees.

If the series is relocated, Dublin's Malahide is the most likely alternative. A cancellation, while unlikely given the financial implications for Cricket Ireland, would deprive the board of its most lucrative home fixture.

## A Community on Edge

For the estimated 7,000 Indians living in Northern Ireland, the unrest has stirred deeper anxieties. While the current protests are not specifically directed at the Indian community, past incidents of racist violence in Belfast have left the diaspora cautious. Community leaders have previously highlighted the vulnerability of South Asian residents during periods of sectarian or anti-immigration tension.

The Indian High Commission in London has not yet issued a travel advisory specifically for Belfast, but NRIs in the region have reported heightened unease on social media. Several have noted that the timing of the cricket series — meant to be a celebration of India's growing sporting relationship with Ireland — now feels incongruous against the backdrop of burning vehicles and riot police.

## The Broader Picture

The Ireland tour is meant to serve as a warm-up for India's larger white-ball series in England, which begins with three ODIs on July 14. The two Belfast T20Is offer India's new T20I leadership — Iyer, Varma, and head coach Gambhir — their first assignment together.

For cricket in Ireland, the stakes extend beyond this series. Cricket Ireland has invested heavily in expanding the sport across the island, and Belfast's inclusion as a venue was a deliberate effort to build audiences in Northern Ireland. A forced relocation or cancellation would set back those plans and raise questions about Belfast's viability as an international cricket venue.

A decision is expected imminently. For now, the Men in Blue wait, and so does a diaspora community that had been looking forward to watching India play in a city many of them call home.

*Sources: Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, Sportscafe.in, BBC News Northern Ireland*
